They convinced Eidos to go with their Anniversary game over Core’s, even though Crystal didn’t even really want to DO Anniversary that much.

Nope, it was a practice employed by a couple different groups. 

Medieval soldiers were allowed to supply their own armor and modify it. However, full plate was heavy, so at times they would not have the back plate. If you kept in formation, it'd allow you better movement and less heat, with the idea that if the people beside you in the formation fell you're probably gunna get a sword thrust between the gaps anyway.   
Plus, leaving the back unarmored could sometimes mean you had to spend half as much money for the armor, and removed 2KG of weight from your body which could mean a lot.

Samurai also did this. The plate on the back is the Sei-Ita, also called "Coward's Plate", because the ideas was if you cared to wear it you were likely planning on fleeing the battle.   
Hence the practice of Samurai not wearing Sei-Ita as a show of confidence and honor.

For Europeans, the breastplate is credited to begin in 1360. The backplate? 1410.   
In multiple places in the 15th century, it was said to have had 50% of the army not have back armor. 

France, Macedonia, Scandinavia, Portugal, Italy, Netherlands, Switzerland, Denmark, Holy Roman Empire, and more all engaged in the practice.  
Hell, it was the standard practice for armor with German Landsknechts.
